scope: Desktop client application implementation review for Windows, macOS, and Linux. No first platform, supported versions, UI technology, or bounded MVP has human approval, and no executable shared domain service exists; this record therefore defines client adapter boundaries and implementation gates without claiming implemented behavior.

dependencyEvidence.sharedBusinessRuleBoundary: Every desktop client consumes one UI-independent download domain service. Clients render durable state and request typed commands; they do not redefine pause, resume, retry, cancellation, destination-conflict, completion, or restart-recovery rules.

clientResponsibilities: Collect URL and destination input through platform-appropriate controls.
Render durable state, progress, user-safe errors, and domain-provided available actions.
Submit commands with the last observed state version and reconcile typed conflict results.
Expose keyboard-operable, named controls and meaningful status through the platform accessibility tree.
Invoke trusted filesystem selection and file-reveal adapters without exposing unrestricted paths to untrusted input.
Restore focus and client selection after dialogs, item removal, command conflicts, and restart recovery.
prohibitedClientRules: Choosing whether cancellation retains partial data
Choosing overwrite, rename, or cancel conflict policy
Marking a download completed before domain finalization
Persisting credentials, signed URL query values, or authorization headers
Automatically opening or executing downloaded content

nativeIntegration: Use the approved Windows file picker and file reveal mechanism.
Validate long paths, locked files, alternate filesystems, atomic rename behavior, and antivirus interaction.
Verify keyboard navigation, visible focus, high contrast, text scaling, and approved Windows screen readers.
Use the approved macOS destination picker and preserve user-granted access according to the chosen sandbox model.
Validate quarantine metadata, case sensitivity, removable destinations, atomic rename behavior, and permission loss.
Verify keyboard operation, Full Keyboard Access, VoiceOver, text scaling, and reduced motion.
Use an approved desktop portal or native picker compatible with the supported packaging model.
Validate permissions, removable volumes, case sensitivity, supported filesystems, atomic rename behavior, and portal denial.
Verify keyboard operation, focus, scaling, reduced motion, and AT-SPI behavior on every supported desktop environment.

clientRuntimeScenarios.scenario: A keyboard-only user adds a valid URL and destination, observes queued and active states, pauses, resumes, completes, and reveals the finalized file.
requiredEvidence: real packaged or development desktop runtime

clientRuntimeScenarios.scenario: The client handles a stale state version by presenting the current durable state and available actions without overwriting the newer transition.
After process termination and restart, queued, paused, failed, interrupted, and completed items are restored; no partial file is represented as completed.
Network loss and invalid resume support produce an accessible interrupted or restart-required outcome, and retry does not silently append incompatible content.
Every approved destination-conflict and cancellation choice states its partial-file consequence, remains keyboard operable, and returns focus to a stable location.
Representative concurrent transfers remain within approved UI-latency, CPU, memory, disk, and network budgets while core controls stay responsive.
requiredEvidence: resource telemetry containing no sensitive URL or credential data

capabilityDisposition.capability: URL intake, destination handling, progress, pause, resume, cancel, retry, completion, file location, and restart recovery
Authenticated downloads, segmented transfers, scheduling, and bandwidth controls

capabilityDisposition.status: not-justified-for-baseline; absent by default unless separately approved with a privacy specification
deferred; current request and architecture define desktop applications only

traceability.limitation: The matrix defines obligations, not an approved platform or implemented client.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15.

blockedBy: A dated human product-owner decision approving the primary segment, first platform, supported OS versions, differentiation, bounded MVP, exclusions, and meaning of all devices
An approved desktop foundation and UI technology with accountable platform ownership
An executable shared download domain service and typed client-facing operations
Approved cancellation, destination-conflict, integrity, persistence, compatibility, and performance policies
Approved packaging, signing, update, rollback, license, governance, vulnerability-reporting, and release-ownership decisions
exitEvidence: Client implementation consuming the shared domain service without duplicated business rules
Automated client adapter tests and shared-domain integration tests
Real desktop runtime keyboard, accessibility-tree, restart, filesystem, and controlled-network evidence
Platform packaging and security evidence for each approved platform

implementationNotes: WS-05 created no speculative application scaffold because the first platform, UI stack, supported versions, MVP policy, and shared service dependency are unresolved.
No database, infrastructure, production, credential, deployment, or Git-history operation was performed.
Source-pattern assertions cannot satisfy the client runtime scenarios; each user-visible claim requires a real DOM, native accessibility tree, desktop integration, or equivalent runtime test.
knownRisks: Choosing a UI framework before native expectations and the first platform are approved could create avoidable rework or inaccessible platform behavior.
Separate client implementations can drift unless all commands, transitions, and policies remain in the shared domain service.
Platform filesystem, accessibility, packaging, signing, and update behavior cannot be inferred from another operating system.
Resume and restart presentation can mislead users or conceal corruption unless it is driven by validated domain and integrity results.
No executable client exists, so runtime accessibility, integration, performance, recovery, and security outcomes remain unverified.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
